overview: This table holds the words shown across shared screens like dialogs, menus, button guides, and license pages, with wording for each supported language.
description: Single unsuffixed table of system UI strings: one FName id plus one FString for each of the 16 supported EApplicationLanguage values (Ja..Th). AGameTextManager routes ids starting with SYS_ (case-insensitively) here from the 14 localized GameText tables, loads this table once regardless of text language, and reads the column selected by the FGameTextRequest language (normally the current UI language).

ID.simple: The name the game uses to find this message in menus, dialogs, and guides.
ID.technical: FName ID reflected column at row +0x00; all 1287 exported rows repeat their row key in ID. Runtime lookup does NOT read this column: GetSystemText calls FindRow<FGameDataTableRow_SystemText> with Request.TextId against the row names of the one unsuffixed SystemTextDataTable. GetText and HasText first test the id string for the SYS_ prefix case-insensitively, so a SYS_ id never falls through to the 14 localized GameText tables even if a GameText row of that name existed. FGameTextRequest(FName) and GetSystemTextById capture GameManager current language; explicit-language FGameTextRequest(id, language[, parameters]) overloads exist. GameTextParameterMap_AddTextId can nest a SYS_ id inside another text as a DYN parameter: it constructs its own request using the then-current language (not an outer request's explicit language) and resolves it through the same prefix split.

Ja.simple: Japanese wording shown in menus, dialogs, and guides when the game uses Japanese.
Ja.technical: FString column returned by GetLanguageText for EApplicationLanguage::Ja (retail jump table maps the enum value to row +0x10 + 0x10 * index). GetSystemText copies the selected column by value using Request.Language and runs FormatText (GLO from the localized glossary cache, DYN from request parameters, tag modifiers). A missing row, an empty cell, or an unmatched language yields an empty FString. The companion export has 1286 of 1287 rows populated. Id-only constructors take the current GameManager language; explicit-language request constructors also exist.

Ar.simple: Arabic wording for language names on the license screen. Most other messages have no Arabic text.
Ar.technical: FString column returned by GetLanguageText for EApplicationLanguage::Ar; GetSystemText reads it only when the request language is Ar, then formats it normally. In the export only 12 rows are populated: SYS_CONFIG_LANGUAGE_LABEL_1001..1011 (shared language names) and SYS_CONFIG_LANGUAGE_LABEL_1012 (Arabic name), used by the license language selector and its language-name text. All other rows are empty, so ordinary Ar requests return empty strings. Only 11 suffix-localized GameText variants exist (in the loader and in Config/DefaultGame.ini:35-45, which assigns them chunks 1-11); there is no Ar GameText shard or chunk rule, and those rows have one Text column rather than per-language columns. AllowedLanguages and GVoiceLanguages do not offer Ar as a UI language in the reconstructed selection code.

notes: FGameDataTableRow_SystemText has 17 reflected UPROPERTY fields (FName ID plus 16 FString language columns). The retail GetLanguageText switch (0x14af7b0 jump table 0x14afb64) maps EApplicationLanguage 0..15 to row +0x10 + 0x10 * index; Invalid = 255 and any unhandled value return an empty FString. The single export holds 1287 rows; every key is uppercase SYS_ and its ID cell matches the key (no repeated or case-insensitively duplicated keys). Populated counts: Ja/En/Fr 1286, Ko 1287, Es/De/It/Pt/Es_LA 1285, Zh_Hant/Zh_Hans 1284, and Ar/Ind/Pl/Ru/Th 12 each. The five sparse columns contain only SYS_CONFIG_LANGUAGE_LABEL_1001..1011 plus their own language-name row (1012..1016); a few individual 11-language rows are blank (for example SYS_CUSTOMIZE_PLAYERCARD_LABEL_0011 in Ja/En/Fr) and resolve to empty text.

Loading differs from the other text groups: StartInitialLoading creates one primary-asset loader for the bare name SystemTextDataTable (GameTextManager.cpp:24), and Tick stores the resolved table in SystemTextDataTables once in state 1 (GameTextManager.cpp:540-544). StartLanguageLoading only unloads/creates the 14 "<Base>_<Language>" GameText loaders; Tick then rebuilds TextDataTables and the glossary-parameter cache and fires OnCultureTextLoaded. The system table and its loader list are not reloaded on a language change (loaders are cleared at GameTextManager.cpp:579), and Config/DefaultGame.ini:35-45 covers only the 11 suffixed GameText chunk variants.

Routing and language selection: IsSystemTextId is a case-insensitive SYS_ prefix test (GameTextManager.cpp:605-607), and GetText/HasText use it with no fallback to GameText rows. GetSystemText reads Request.Language at GameTextManager.cpp:718; id-only requests and GetSystemTextById use the GameManager current language, while explicit-language FGameTextRequest overloads (GameTextRequest.h:97-100) are the only way to override it. Widget ids applied with EApplicationLanguage::Invalid take the current-language path (GameWidgetButton.cpp:103-120). Nested text-id parameters build their own current-language request when added (GameTextManager.cpp:406, 810), so a SYS_ id nested in another string is resolved by the same split but does not inherit an outer explicit language.

Formatting: GetSystemText passes the copied column, request parameters, and the glossary cache to FormatText (GameTextManager.cpp:720, 724-805). GLO tags read GlossaryParameters (rebuilt from GlossaryTextDataTable_<Language>); DYN tags read the request map; recognized modifiers are ABS, RATE_TO_PCT, FULL_WIDTH, HALF_WIDTH and DECIMAL_PLACE_1..4. The export itself contains 412 GLO/126 DYN tags in Ja and 166 GLO/126 DYN in En (plus one misspelled <DNY=ITEM> row that the formatter leaves literal); Chinese columns additionally use DYN=FRIEND_WORD/FREND_LIST_WORD, for which FormatText injects GLS_GAME_WORDS_3000/3004 based on the current language. GroupDigits (GameTextManager.cpp:200-222) resolves SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0124/0123/0122 for 2/3/4 three-digit blocks with BLOCK_%02d parameters (1 or more than 4 blocks are returned unchanged); decimal points use SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0121 with INTEGER/DECIMAL parameters (GameTextManager.cpp:270, 362).

Consumers reach rows directly through GetText/GetSystemTextById and indirectly through widget text interfaces and id-valued fields in other tables. C++ literals name 606 distinct complete SYS_ ids present in the export; aliases include ArcadeMissionSetDataTable.Id_Text_Title and MainMenuThemeDataTable.Id_Text, while the SYS_ sound ids in SoundEffectDataTable are separate SE_SYS_ cues and are not text rows. HasText also handles SYS_ ids, but FindTextIdsContaining and HasGameTextContent only scan the GameText tables, so there is no manager API to enumerate system ids. Partial Content means additional retail/Blueprint-assigned ids cannot be enumerated.

Verification caveat: status/functions.json byte-matches GetSystemText (0x14af7b0), GetText (0x14afde0), GetSystemTextById (0x14afbb0/0x14afcd0), FormatText (0x14c4870) and GroupDigits (0x14b0df0). The row finder 0x14af3d0 is behaviour-certified by BEHAV AU02 and Tick 0x14c96f0 by BEHAV BG03. The GetLanguageText helper and reflected field names are reconstructed; no retail Blueprint evidence is available beyond partial Content, so only traced C++ consumers are asserted.

usages.detail: Creates the sole primary-asset loader for the unsuffixed SystemTextDataTable at initial load.
Caches the resolved table in SystemTextDataTables once; later language loads replace only the 14 GameText tables.
SYS_ prefix test (case-insensitive) sends ids to the system table and prevents GameText fallback.
FindRow on the cached table by Request.TextId and GetLanguageText(Request.Language); missing row yields an empty string.
Formats the copied string with GLO/DYN modifiers using request parameters and the glossary cache.
GroupDigits resolves SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0122..0124 with BLOCK_01..04 for thousands separators.
Decimal-point formatting for string parameters uses SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0121 with INTEGER/DECIMAL.
A text-id parameter re-enters GetText with its own request; GameTextParameterMap_AddTextId can point it at a SYS_ row.
Nests SYS_PVE_MATCH_SELECT_LABEL_0112 as a LIMIT parameter of a system dialog message (the mirror branch at line 1032 uses _0111).
Resolves SYS_DIALOG_MESSAGE_0301 with a nested MISSION_NAME text id for story chapter/mission lists.
Uses label alias index 1 (SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0104, "<DYN=TIME> second(s)") with TIME = int-truncated seconds from Global::TimeLimit; index 2 is the infinite-time label SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0032.
Maps free-battle time label keys 1 and 2 to SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0104 and SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0032.
Formats SYS_COMMON_LABEL_0104 with TIME seconds from Global->TimeLimit[0]/[1] and adds SYS_COMMON_LABEL_1315 for unlimited.
GLanguageLabels maps the 11 selectable UI languages to SYS_CONFIG_LANGUAGE_LABEL_1001..1011.
Merges the 11 language labels with the five extra labels 1012..1016 for the license language selector.
Sets the displayed license language name from the merged SYS_CONFIG_LANGUAGE_LABEL map.
Uses ArcadeMissionSetDataTable.Id_Text_Title, whose exported values are SYS_ARCADE_ROOT_SELECT_ROOT_LABEL_*.
Uses MainMenuThemeDataTable.Id_Text, whose exported values are SYS_MAIN_MENU_THEME_LABEL_0101..0103.
With bForceOneLine, newline removal/space substitution depends on the current UI language, not the table column.
